character: Two voices, a couple at the kitchen bench on a Sunday night. MEL (white captions): everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, the same Mel as 'Which Dave?', renovating the main bathroom in Hamilton. Dry, under-played, a little bit pleased with herself; she reads the screen out loud the way you'd explain it to your partner, never sells, never says what QSME 'did for her' (no testimonial). HIM (green bubbles): her partner, relaxed Kiwi bloke, late 30s to 40s, low and flat, bone-dry. He asked the question, he'd have picked the wrong quote, and he's fine with that: the joke is on the GST formats and a bit on himself, never on the tradies. General NZ accents, natural and unhurried, never broad, never Australian, no announcer lift, no exclamation marks. Both are AI voices of fictional people: never presented as real customers.

voices.Mel: tools/voices.json → qsme-nz.voice_id (Jenna, NZ female; casting in projects/2026-10-02-qsme-voice-casting)

casting_line: Three quotes for one bathroom, and every one of them wrote GST differently. Course they did.

post_processing: Time base: every time is seconds on outputs/which-ones-cheapest-9x16.mp4 (31.6 s). outputs/which-ones-cheapest-4x5.mp4 runs on the same clock, so one VO/SFX/music stem fits both.

Two voices: tools/make_vo.py voices every line in 'lines' with ONE voice, so do not use --all for this project. Generate Mel's lines with the qsme-nz voice_id and Him's lines (vo01, vo08, vo11) with the qsme-nz alt_voice_id, one request per line with previous_text/next_text set to the neighbouring lines of the SAME speaker. Pick takes by ear, save them as <line id>.mp3 in one folder, then lay them with: python3 tools/make_vo.py projects/2026-10-20-qsme-nz-apples-oranges-pineapple --files <folder> (writes outputs/which-ones-cheapest-9x16-with-vo.mp4). Repeat the mux for the 4:5 file with tools/mux and the same start times.

vo04 and vo05 are one sentence split across two captions: generate them as ONE request ('The emailed one goes in too, after I've checked it.') and cut at the comma, keeping the natural pause; place the second half at 8.38.
Trim leading/trailing digital silence. Never time-stretch more than about 4%; if a take runs past max_s, use another take.
Breaths: keep a quiet inhale before vo03, vo06 and vo12 (after silences), pulled down 6 to 10 dB; cut mouth clicks. vo13 is a J-cut: it starts 0.34 s before the end-card cut.
Mix: the VO sits on top; music ducks 6 dB under each line. SFX (paper slaps, marker squeak, cup clacks, toggle click) are never under a word.
AI disclosure: if ElevenLabs voices ship, switch on each platform's AI-generated content label.
